# TrustBazaar build progress

This file is the single record of what is being built, by whom, and what is finished. Read `BUILDING.md` first. Every pull request that starts, finishes or blocks a task updates this file in the same pull request. `python3 scripts/check_progress.py` checks it (CI runs it too).

**Status values:** `todo` · `doing` (owner and branch set) · `review` (pull request open) · `done` (pull request merged) · `blocked` (reason in Notes).

**Rules:** take tasks only when everything in *Needs* is `done` · one owner per task · do not edit another owner's `doing` row without asking · a design question goes to the Decisions log, never silently into code.

## U11: Code health (clean-up and a design system)

Added on 2026-11-27 at the user's request. Aim: the code can be read and changed by another developer. Every kind of thing on the site (a card, a button, a progress line, a field, a popup) exists once, as a component with variants that adapts to its place; a page supplies only the content and the situation (a buyer and a seller get different steps and words from data, drawn by the same component); colours, fonts, spacing and the like come from one set of tokens, so changing one changes the whole site. No task changes what a screen shows or does. Screenshots before and after are identical (U11-02, U11-03, U11-10), or differ only where the inventory (U11-13) chose one canonical value for what existed in several versions (the primitives, U11-04 and U11-05); every such difference is listed in its pull request with before and after images. Order: frontend first, then backend. Plan and numbers: Decisions log, 2026-11-27, U11.

## Decisions log

Any change to the design made while building: what, why, who agreed, and which document must be updated.

| Date | Task | Decision | Agreed by | Document to update |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-31 | P0-02 | CI `reference-browser`: run `apt-get update` before `apt-get install -y nginx-light`; without it the runner's stale package index asks for a version the mirror no longer has (404). Applied to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the reference `docs/design/deploy/github/workflows/ci.yml`. | S. M. Nihal Ahmed; reviewer of #35 | Unit 9 (`09_integration.tex`) if it quotes the CI steps |
| 2026-10-31 | P0-03 | `CODEOWNERS`: the security paths (`identity/`, `orders/`, `game-accounts/`) are owned by all three team members (any one non-author approval suffices); the old `* @nihal4` rule is removed, since the branch rule already requires a non-author review on every PR. `/.github/` is added to the security paths so CI and `CODEOWNERS` cannot be weakened by an ordinary review. | S. (5) Strikes are append-only and unique per order and reason; seller and buyer strikes are counted apart (`trust.record_strike` now counts seller reasons only, `trust.record_buyer_strike` buyer reasons only), so a buyer strike never suspends selling and a seller strike never counts against buying. (6) The buyer is told in the dispute chat. THE RETURN CHECK: for an item with a device identifier the seller types the identifier of the item taken back (`POST /disputes/{id}/return-check`; only the result is kept, `disputes.return_checks`); `return-received` needs a matching check; a mismatch opens a `return_mismatch` signal and leaves only the operator's way out, `POST /staff/disputes/{id}/resolve-return` (`refund` completes the return, `release` rejects it and pays the seller), allowed on a mismatch or once the decision target has passed, so no refund can hang on the seller and no seller can block it by mistyping. The limits (2 strikes, 365 days) are fixed in the code, not a parameter. NOT BUILT: the seller's screen for the return check and the staff screens (no staff console yet; the API and the chat texts exist); lifting a buyer strike (strikes cannot be removed; a suspension is lifted through the existing sanction lift with four-eyes); a courier return cannot be checked (nothing to type for a parcel). | the user | SRS FR-TNS-10 |

| 2026-11-28 | U11-11 | THE BACKEND CLEAN-UP. (1) THE INTEGRATION SUITE, the safety net, was run on my own machine against a throw-away PostgreSQL and Redis in containers on other ports (the dev database is never touched), set up as CI does it (the init script, the migrations as tb_owner, the tests as tb_app): 117 suites and 723 tests pass, three times, in about 3 minutes. THE INTERMITTENT HANG (the integration job failing at about 10 minutes on PR #320 and #326): NOT REPRODUCED, and this is said plainly. What was found: the app used the default pool of 10 connections with no wait limit, a transaction holds one connection for its whole length, and the code itself documents the hazard (`second-chance.service.ts`, U1-10: a read that needs a second pool connection while the transaction holds the auction's lock can wait for ever when every connection waits for that lock); the failing test fires exactly 10 requests at once. Neither a pool of 2 nor a database throttled to half a CPU reproduced it, so the cause is a timing-dependent starvation that is likely but unproven. WHAT WAS DONE, so that the class is removed and the next occurrence explains itself: the pool is configurable and has headroom (`DB_POOL_MAX`, default 20, was the library's 10); a request waits at most `DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 20 s, was for ever) for a connection and then fails with an error instead of hanging for minutes and poisoning every later suite; a watchdog (`kernel/db/pool-watch.ts`) logs a warning when requests wait with no connection free and an error when it lasts, with the numbers; unit-tested. If the job hangs again its log now says why. (2) UNUSED CODE: 5 unused dependencies removed (`@nestjs/config`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `@nestjs/passport`, `passport`, `passport-jwt`: the sign-in is our own cookie code) and `express`, which two specs import, is now a dev dependency; knip's unused exports went from 165 to 81 and unused types from 19 to 8: 94 exports that are used inside their own file only lost their `export`, 3 declarations used nowhere were deleted, and the entity barrels and the modules' ports were left alone (TypeORM loads the entities; the ports are each module's public contract); a type used in a public method's signature must stay exported (the compiler said so once). (3) OPENAPI, a MUST requirement never delivered (IF-COM-04; NFR-MNT-05 says generated from the code): `docs/api/openapi.json`, 3.1.0, 231 operations on 207 paths, 93 request schemas, generated by `backend/test/support/openapi.ts` from the real routes, the policy decorators, the class-validator rules of the DTOs and the doc comments; the integration job fails when the file is stale or a route has no description; it does not describe the shape of a successful answer yet (it says so). `docs/api/README.md` tells how to keep it and how to add a route. (4) COMMENTS: the 53 operations and 93 public service methods that had none now have a sentence (written from reading each handler; where a detail was not certain it is not claimed). (5) LIMITS as errors in `.eslintrc.js`, just above the largest the code has (a file 720 lines of code, a function 160, complexity 50), to come down as the large services are split.
